title: What do you do for a living?
title_target: Ким ви працюєте? — Kym vy pratsyuyete?
goal: Ask about and name jobs, say the verb "to work" in all six forms, and meet the fifth case (орудний, the instrumental) through its easiest doorway: jobs always use it.
bekal: ask about someone's job with Ким?
say what you and your family do
put job names into the орудний
conjugate працювати in all six forms

dialogs.title: Діалог — After class, in the cafeteria
dialogs.intro: Ani and Andriy are having lunch. Look at the first line: Ani calls Andriy by the calling form, **Андрію** — not *Андрій*. Notice too that every job name ends in a brand-new sound.

lines.speaker: Андрій:
lines.id: I work as a waiter in a café. And you?
lines.literal: I — work — waiter (орудний) — in — café. and — you?

lines.speaker: Ані:
lines.id: I'm not working yet. Just studying.
lines.literal: I — for-now — not — work. only — study.

lines.speaker: Андрій:
lines.id: What about your parents? What do they do?
lines.literal: and — your — parents? as-whom — they — work?

lines.speaker: Ані:
lines.id: Mom works as a teacher, and Dad's an engineer.
lines.literal: mom — works — teacher (f, орудний), and — dad — engineer (орудний).

lines.speaker: Андрій:
lines.id: Interesting! Where does your mom work?

lines.speaker: Ані:
lines.id: Very much. She says it's the best job in the world.
lines.literal: very. she — says, that — this — best — work — in — world.

lines.speaker: Андрій:
lines.id: Then your mom is a lucky person.

notes: **Ким?, not Хто?** *Хто ти?* asks who you are (your identity). *Ким ти працюєш?* asks what you work as. The correct answer to the second question **must** use the орудний: *офіціантом*, not *офіціант*.

**The орудний endings are -ом, -ем, or -ою.** Masculine nouns ending in a hard consonant → **-ом** (*інженер* → *інженером*). Ending in a soft consonant or -й → **-ем** (*водій* → *водієм*, *лікар* → *лікарем*). Feminine nouns in -а → **-ою** (*вчителька* → *вчителькою*).

**Працювати follows the first pattern, but its stem shrinks.** The dictionary form is *працювати*, but once you conjugate it, **-юва-** collapses to **-ю-**: *я працюю*, not *я працюваю*. Every verb ending in **-увати / -ювати** behaves the same way: *малювати* → *малюю*, *дякувати* → *дякую*.
**Поки не = not yet, for now.** Softer than *ще ні* because it implies the situation is temporary. *Я поки не працюю* — I'm not working yet (but I will be).

**Вчуся is a reflexive verb.** The ending **-ся** originally meant "oneself": *вчити* = to teach, *вчитися* = to teach oneself, i.e. to study. You'll meet this group again in Unit 12; for now just remember *я вчуся*, *ти вчишся*.

**Job names have feminine forms, and people use them.** *Вчитель* / *вчителька*, *лікар* / *лікарка*, *студент* / *студентка*, *перекладач* / *перекладачка*. Unlike some European languages that have dropped feminine forms, Ukrainian is actively reviving them.

**У світі, not в світі.** After a consonant people use *у*; after a vowel, *в*. It's the same ease-of-speech habit as з / із / зі in Unit 3, and once again: picking the wrong one never stops anyone understanding you.

grammars.title: Працювати in six forms
body: First pattern, with **-ю-** in the stem. Learn this table and you've got dozens of other verbs ending in -увати too.

grammars.title: Jobs in the орудний
body: The second column is what you use after *працювати*. The first column is only for sentences with no verb: *Він лікар.*
after: Look at **продавець** → **продавцем**: the **е** in the last syllable drops out as soon as the ending changes. All words ending in **-ець** behave this way (*українець* → *українцем*).

blocks.text: To say **at / in** a place, Ukrainian uses в/у or на, and the place goes into the sixth case (місцевий, the locative). The ending is almost always **-і**. This case is covered fully in Unit 10; for now, just learn the pairs.
The last two rows use **на**, not **в**. There's no really tidy rule for this — *на роботі*, *на заводі*, *на пошті*, *на вокзалі* have to be learned one by one. Luckily there aren't many.

blocks.title: Three ways to ask about someone's job
items: **Ким ви працюєте?** — the most common and the safest. Literally "as whom do you work".
**Хто ви за професією?** — a bit more formal; it sounds like a question on a form. Literally "who are you by profession".
**Де ви працюєте?** — asks about the place, not the position. You answer with *у школі*, *в офісі*, not a job title.
⚠️ If you're not working yet, the most natural answer isn't silence but **Я ще вчуся** (I'm still at school / university) or **Я поки не працюю**.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the blanks with the correct орудний form.
Fill in the blanks with the right form of працювати.
Put the words in the right order.

items: What do you do for a living? (formal)
My mother works as a teacher.
I'm not working yet. I'm still studying.

answers: Ким ти працюєш? — Я працюю у кафе. — Я поки не працюю. — Моя мама працює вчителькою. — Це гарна робота.
Ким ви працюєте? — Я працюю лікарем. — Моя мама працює вчителькою. — Я поки не працюю. Я ще вчуся. — Їй подобається її робота.
